Keep a private key mapping platform identifiers to random participant IDs

Source: R/rawdata-id-key.R
update_id_key.Rd

Replaces platform identifiers, such as JATOS study result IDs, with random participant identifiers, so that no data bundle and nothing derived from one, carries an identifier that links back to the platform and, through it, to e-mail addresses or start times. The key lives in the private folder and grows with every call, with identifiers seen before keeping their participant ID and new ones getting fresh random IDs.

Usage

update_id_key(ids, file, prefix = NULL, dir = Sys.getenv("CATLAS_PRIVATE_DIR"))

Arguments

ids

Platform identifiers, one per study result, e.g. the id_sr column of pull_jatos_batches(). Coerced to character. Must not contain NA.

file

Character(1). Path of the key file within the private folder, e.g. "fba-allergy-online-02/id-key.rds". It must be an .rds file.

prefix

Character(1), NA or NULL. Prefix of the participant IDs. NULL (default) and NA prepend no prefix.

dir

Character(1). The private folder. Defaults to the environment variable CATLAS_PRIVATE_DIR, which belongs in .Renviron.

Value

A character vector of participant IDs, of the same length and in the same order as ids.

Details

Call this function before building any bundle, writing any coding file or recording any exclusion.

Participant IDs

A participant ID is a random six-digit number, e.g. "482913", preceded by prefix if one is given (e.g. "p482913"), drawn without replacement among those not yet in the key. The number never starts with zero, so that spreadsheet programs, which drop leading zeros of numbers, cannot alter an ID in the debriefing coding file. Unlike sequential numbers, such as JATOS's id_sr, the CATLAS participant IDs do not contain any information about the order or the time of participation.

Randomness

The digits are drawn from a freshly initialised random number generator, so that they do not depend on any seed set in the calling script, because anyone with the correct seed and the platform identifiers could rebuild the key otherwise. The state of the session's generator is restored after the IDs are generated. The key file makes the IDs reproducible, so losing it breaks the link between later pulls and earlier IDs.

The key

A tibble with the columns source_id (the platform identifier, as character), id (the participant ID) and assigned_at (UTC), saved in the private folder, with the guards of write_private_rds(), whenever new identifiers arrive. Like every private file, it must never enter a repository.

See also

write_private_rds(), read_private_rds()
